# Third-party notices

**Generated file — do not edit by hand.** Regenerate with `scripts/gen-notice.sh`;
`--check` fails CI when it is stale. See `NOTICE` for the copyright statement,
the source-code written offer, and how to exercise it.

This inventory is read out of the **built images**, not the manifests, because
the image is what a user receives. Debian components come from each package's
machine-readable `/usr/share/doc/<pkg>/copyright` (DEP-5).

## GPL-family components carry a source obligation

Distributing these binaries obliges us to provide the complete corresponding
source. `NOTICE` carries the written offer that discharges it. FFmpeg is the
significant one: Debian builds it `--enable-gpl`, making the binaries GPL-2+
(GPL-3+ for the libavcodec/libavfilter flavour). It is invoked as a subprocess,
so this is aggregation and does **not** place our own code under the GPL.

## AGPL-3.0 components — the strongest obligation here

These are **not** ordinary GPL. AGPL-3.0 extends the source obligation to
users who interact with the software **over a network**, so operating a
modified version as a service triggers it even where nothing is distributed:

- `ultralytics` 8.4.144 — AGPL-3.0, in **analytics**
- `ultralytics-platform` 0.1.33 — AGPL-3.0-only, in **analytics**
- `ultralytics-thop` 2.1.6 — AGPL-3.0, in **analytics**

This is compatible with the project as it stands, because the images above
ship under AGPL-3.0 themselves. It would **not** be compatible if that
functionality moved behind a paid tier — AGPL is a one-way door. The code
keeps that door narrow on purpose: the detector is a single class behind a
`Detector` protocol, so replacing it with an Apache-2.0 model is one new
class and one line of configuration. See the header of
`services/analytics/analytics/detector.py`.

## Vendored in the repository

Committed directly to this repository and therefore distributed by the SOURCE
release, before any image exists. No package manager reports them, so their
licences come from `vendored-licenses.tsv`, whose completeness `gen-notice.sh`
enforces — an undeclared file under `vendor/` fails the run.

They appear in the inventory above marked *vendored in repo*. `UNKNOWN` in a
version column means the artifact carries no determinable version and needs
confirming against upstream before publishing.
